module purpose: Processor-internal instruction memory: accepts bus requests (bus_req_i), maps the bus address to an internal index, returns a 32-bit word on bus_rsp_o.data and an acknowledge on bus_rsp_o.ack, and (when configured as RAM) accepts per-byte writes into mem_ram_b0..b3. Sequencing uses clk_i and rstn_i.

use-case flows.value: Per-byte writes into instruction RAM: bus_req_i.data -> mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 at addr when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1'), gated by bus_req_i.ben bits (RAM builds only).
Instruction fetch: select a 32-bit word from ROM or RAM into rdata and present it on bus_rsp_o.data when rden = '1'.
Acknowledge the bus request: bus_rsp_o.ack is driven from bus_req_i.stb (and, for IMEM_INIT=true, from (not bus_req_i.rw)).
Reset clears response state: rstn_i = '0' forces rden <= '0' and bus_rsp_o.ack <= '0'.

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction memory contents — the 32-bit instruction words the block holds and delivers to requesters
conceptual assets.reasoning: The delivered word is produced from rdata which the RTL loads from either the pre-initialized ROM or from the RAM byte registers and then drives out. ROM read: rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr)) on clk edge (line 81) or via addr_ff when alt_style (line 95). RAM read: rdata(7 downto 0) <= mem_ram_b0(to_integer(addr)) etc. (lines 128–131 and alt-style 159–162). The output bus_rsp_o.data is derived from rdata when (rden = '1') (line 185). These RTL statements and the map records (rdata SELECTED_BY mem_rom_c / mem_ram_b* and bus_rsp_o.data DERIVES_FROM rdata) establish that the integrity of fetched instructions depends on the stored ROM/RAM bytes and the rdata register. (Note: mem_rom_c is a compile-time initializer constant and not a SIGNAL in the closed set; the run-time registers and the exit port are listed below.)

conceptual assets.concept: Writable instruction memory — the ability for bus writes to modify IMEM bytes (RAM builds)
conceptual assets.reasoning: When IMEM_INIT = false the mem_access process writes bus_req_i.data bytes into mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 under the condition (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1') and per-byte enables bus_req_i.ben (lines 113–126 for non-alt_style, 139–156 for alt_style). The map shows mem_ram_b* are updated (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and those updates are guarded (GATED_BY) by bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.ben and sourced from bus_req_i.data. Therefore the integrity of stored program bytes depends on these write conditions and the incoming data and enables.

conceptual assets.concept: Effective memory index — the internal address used to select which memory word is read or written
conceptual assets.reasoning: The file maps the bus address into an internal index via addr <= unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(addr_hi_c downto 2)) (line 101). The latched index addr_ff (assigned in clocked mem_access when alt_style is chosen at lines 92 and 142) can be used to select rdata (map shows SELECTED_BY records on addr and addr_ff). Corrupting the address or its mapping would cause accesses to target the wrong memory location, breaking fetch and write correctness.

conceptual assets.concept: Read-response control — the stored read-enable (rden) and the outgoing acknowledge (bus_rsp_o.ack) that govern delivery of fetch results
conceptual assets.reasoning: bus_feedback sets rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 176) and drives bus_rsp_o.ack from bus_req_i.stb (and, when IMEM_INIT = true, from bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw)) (lines 177–180). rden gates the output data (bus_rsp_o.data <= rdata when (rden = '1') else zeros) (line 185). The map records show rden as a CLOCKED register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, RESET_BY rstn_i) and bus_rsp_o.ack as a driven output with GATED_BY records referencing bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw. Thus the correctness (integrity) and availability of read responses depend on these stored and driven control values.
